title: Launch Stability Commander — Runlist and KPI Gazette
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, practical runlist for the Launch Stability Commander role for the next major product rollout (internal staging -> limited public). Goal: keep API latency and error-rate within SLOs while we scale from pilot traffic to 50k daily requests.

Context / scope:
- Audience: product-ops, oncall SRE, release engineers, solutions-eng for customer pilots.
- Target window: phased rollout over 6 weeks (canary -> 10% -> 50% -> full), with daily checkpoints for first 14 days.
- Primary risks: model-serving throughput regressions, KV cache thrash, sudden token-cost spike from prompt regressions.

Quick summary for execs (1 line):
- Keep latency p50 < 120ms, p95 < 350ms, errors < 0.5% during ramp; automated fallback to cheap variant at 1% error above baseline.

Key owners (hand-off matrix):
- Stability Commander (primary): Elena Park (product-ops) — overall run lead, decision authority for traffic shifts.
- SRE oncall (technical): Marcus Liu — infra scaling, autoscaler overrides, rollback.
- Serving runtime eng: Ravi Menon — per-model perf regressions, kernel selection issues.
- Solutions / CS pilot owner: Ana Gómez — customer communication and acceptance criteria.
- Product PM: Sophie Kane — product signal owner and canary criteria.

Readiness signals (green / amber / red):
- Latency (p95)
  - Green: p95 < 350ms for 30m window
  - Amber: p95 350–500ms; investigate batching, KV hit-rate, queueing
  - Red: p95 > 500ms for 10m -> scale down rollout, enable fallback variant
- Error rate (4xx+5xx endpoints)
  - Green: < 0.5%
  - Amber: 0.5%–1.5% (triage route-level error spikes)
  - Red: > 1.5% sustained 5m -> pause rollout, run triage runbook
- Cost per 1k tokens (observed)
  - Green: within 10% of forecast
  - Amber: +10–25% -> check prompt regressions / token inflation
  - Red: > +25% -> evaluate quantized variant and burst routing
- Quality degradation (automated evals on held prompts)
  - Green: eval delta <= -0.5% relative to baseline
  - Amber: -0.5% to -2% -> alert ML/product for immediate review
  - Red: <= -2% -> rollback model or reduce traffic to baseline

KPI watchlist (dashboard columns & thresholds):
- Traffic slice (canary/10%/50%/full) — owners update every cadence tick
- Request/sec by region and model variant
- Latency p50/p95/p99 (global + per-model)
- Error rate (5xx + model-failure categories)
- KV cache hit rate and reuse ratio
- Average tokens per request and token surge events
- Cost per 1k tokens and 30m rolling average
- Canary eval pass rate (automated prompt-suite)

Action playbooks (short):
- If amber latency:
  - Check autoscaler headroom (SRE) -> add nodes or increase burst limit
  - Inspect batching queue lengths (serving runtime) -> temporarily reduce batch window
  - Toggle reduced-batching mode on hot routes
- If red latency or red error rate:
  - Pause traffic ramp immediately (Stability Commander)
  - Flip traffic to fallback variant or lower-capacity cheaper model
  - Create P1 incident, page SRE + runtime + product PM
  - Reproduce locally with recent traces, attach to incident ticket
- If cost spike amber->red:
  - Run token audit (use console trace) -> find route with prompt drift
  - Throttle or route high-token paths to dedicated reserved pools where possible
  - Consider model quantization profile swap (with ML approval)

Canary plan (practical steps):
- Phase 0: smoke in staging (internal-only) — run 24h, validate eval suite, smoke errors <0.1%
- Phase 1: closed pilot (selected customers) 6–12h slices, manual monitoring by Stability Commander
- Phase 2: 10% public traffic 24–48h, automated gating at each 6h checkpoint
- Phase 3: 50% 48–72h if green, otherwise iterate on partial rollback
- Phase 4: full release after 7 days of stable 50% metrics and no major regressions

Staffing & rotations (first 14 days intensive):
- Stability Commander shifts: 0800–2000 PT daily first 7 days; then 0900–1700 PT through day 14
- Oncall SRE 24/7 primary: Marcus Liu (week 1), backup: Priya Shah
- Runtime eng standby: Ravi (daytime), rotate with Aaron for overlaps
- CS pilot contact: Ana — pager for customer-impact alerts only

Prelaunch checklist (go/no-go gate for canary):
- [ ] Release artifact validated and pinned in model catalog
- [ ] Canary eval suite run with zero critical failures
- [ ] Autoscaling policy verified for expected QPS (2x buffer)
- [ ] Cost forecast updated for initial 14-day window and committed budget owner tagged
- [ ] Rollback plan documented (variant id, traffic reweight script)
- [ ] Stakeholder comms draft ready (CS/Legal/comms)

Telemetry and dashboards (what to watch live):
- Console: per-token cost widget, p95 latency commit chart
- Grafana: routing queues, node CPU/GPU utilization, batch window distribution
- Tracing: sample traces for p95 tail; attach recent prompts/response lengths
- Canary eval: daily rollup email of pass/fail and top 10 failures

Post-launch: first 90 days roadmap (metrics & cadence):
- Day 0–14 (stabilize): hourly reviews for first 72h, then 6h cadence; retention of step logs
- Week 3–4 (optimize): implement batching/quantization suggestions from Optimize team; measure cost delta
- Month 2 (scale tests): run stress tests 2x target RPS in staging; validate autoscaler behaviour
- Month 3 (hand-off): shift to standard oncall rotations and reduce Stability Commander intensity; produce final runbook edits

Open questions / decisions pending:
- Should we enable cross-region routing fallback at 10%? (Pros: resilience; Cons: data residency implications for some pilots)
- Acceptance threshold for customer-facing latency (some customers require p95 < 250ms)
- Funding approval for dedicated reserved capacity if 50% ramp sustained -> timeline to commit

Notes to self / rough TODOs:
- Add link to runbook snippets for 'toggle reduced-batching' command
- Confirm canary eval suite contains edge prompts from Solutions-eng (ask Ana)
- Draft short FAQ for pilot customers about possible transient throttling
- Follow up with ML on quantization check for top-3 heavy routes (Ravi)

Appendix: immediate runlist for next 8 hours (day of canary start):
- T minus 120m: final artifact pin + smoke run (Sophie + Elena)
- T minus 60m: verify autoscaler & node health (Marcus)
- T minus 30m: notify pilot customers + oncall roster confirm (Ana)
- T plus 0m: shift 1% traffic to canary, start 10m golden metrics window
- T plus 10m: check p95 and error rate; if green continue to 1h window; if amber invoke amber steps
- T plus 60m: escalate to 10% if metrics stable

End.

Draft history: informal working doc — slightly choppy, intended for iteration. Last edited by Elena Park on 2026-02-15."
